projects.name: E-Social: Leveraging Digital Solutions to Enable Efficient Social Protection of the Vulnerable
projects.description:
UNDP has supported the Government of Montenegro in establishing the national Integrated Social Welfare Information System (e-Social IS), which has been in operation since January 2015. Being the backbone of the country's social protection system, e-Social is in charge of processing nearly all social protection entitlements. 

To provide timely and efficiently cash transfers and social services and to ensure that new legislative solutions are duly enforced, it is necessary to continuously invest in the e-Social IS. To that end, the project envisages key components, including the development of new and upgraded functionalities (including its e-services for citizens), IS refactoring, capacity-building support for IS administrators and end-users, as well as its maintenance to ensure medium-term sustainability. The project will also provide, until 31 December 2027, procurement of additional server capacities as well as regular hardware supply replacement and maintenance in 36 remote locations.

projects.name: Support to the Reform of Disability Assessment and Introduction of the Inclusive Allowance
projects.description: In Montenegro, persons with disabilities continue to face systemic barriers that limit their full participation in social, economic, and public life. The project aims to consolidate and operationalize Montenegro’s transition to a unified, human-rights–based disability assessment and social protection system. Building on the achievements of Phase I (2020–2025), the project will move from legal and policy formulation to implementation—translating the newly adopted Law on Unified Disability Assessment into practice and introducing the Inclusive Allowance as a single, needs-based cash benefit for persons with disabilities. By combining legal reform, institutional capacity development, and digital innovation, the project will complete Montenegro’s transition to a modern, inclusive, and rights-based disability determination and social protection system. It will enable more than 60,000 persons with disabilities to access their rights more easily and equitably, while enhancing the efficiency, transparency, and accountability of public institutions in line with the UN CRPD, EU accession commitments, and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Project specifically supports implementation of Reform Agenda measure 3.1.3 Reforming social and child protection system for more effective, efficient, and transparent use of public funds specifically step 3: One single inclusive and unified disability-related cash transfer covering all rights of a given beneficiary and processed through an electronic system in place.

projects.name: Enhance strategic frameworks for the AFOLU sectors and support the initiation of the second National Forest Inventory of Montenegro
projects.description:
Despite progress in resilience building, Montenegro faces data deficits and lacks specific baseline information and monitoring systems for effective climate planning. This gap hinders the integration of AFOLU sectors into the NDC update and future climate strategies. Without enhanced data collection and inter-sectoral cooperation, Montenegro risks failing to meet its climate targets and commitments.
The Readiness Proposal aims to address these gaps by improving data collection and institutional capacities. Key barriers include limited multi-stakeholder dialogue, insufficient specific data and monitoring systems, lack of awareness among national institutions, outdated forest inventory methodologies, and limited private sector engagement in climate investment. This initiative seeks to improve Montenegro’s ability to respond to climate challenges by enhancing data collection, fostering multi-stakeholder cooperation, and building institutional capacities. These efforts are crucial for achieving the country’s climate goals and ensuring sustainable development in the face of increasing climate impacts.

projects.name: Support to UNEP/MAP-GEF-Funded MedProgramme for Removal of PCB and Mercury Wastes in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Tunisia (UNEP/MAP-GEF-Funded MedProgramme)
projects.description:
Under the GEF-funded MedProgramme, two complementary activities were implemented for Montenegro during the 2025–2026 period, addressing priority chemical pollution hotspots and supporting the environmentally sound management of persistent organic pollutants.

The first activity concerns the implementation of a Small-Scale Funding Agreement focused on the environmental assessment of contamination at the Port of Bar. This SSFA represents a continuation of earlier assessment work conducted in Montenegro, which examined contamination levels in harbour sediments at Tivat Bay and Risan Harbour. The previous SSFA included the analysis of PCBs, mercury, other heavy metals and organic substances, and revealed contaminant concentrations exceeding threshold values at specific sampling points in Tivat Bay. These findings highlighted the need for further site-specific assessment and potential remediation measures. Building on this evidence base, the current SSFA aims to further characterize contamination at the Port of Bar while also supporting the development of an environmental sound management plan for monitoring and remediation actions in Tivat Bay. Through this activity, Montenegro contributes to Component 1, Output 1.1 of the GEF MedProgramme Child Project 1.1, which targets the management of persistent organic pollutants in identified Mediterranean hotspots, in line with the UNEP/MAP Programme of Work and Budget.

The second activity is implemented through an Implementing Partner Services Agreement between UNEP/MAP and UNOPS and focuses on the environmentally sound management and disposal of PCB waste in Montenegro. Under this regional agreement, approximately 77 tons of PCB-contaminated equipment and oils from Montenegro are being safeguarded, collected, transported and exported for environmentally sound disposal in compliance with international standards, including the Basel Convention. This activity forms part of a wider regional effort covering Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Tunisia, contributing to the phase-out and elimination of PCBs by March 2026 under Child Project 1.1. The agreement supports Montenegro’s obligations under the Stockholm Convention, where PCBs are listed as persistent organic pollutants due to their severe impacts on human health and the environment.

Implementation of the IPS Agreement follows a coordinated approach between UNEP/MAP and UNOPS. UNEP/MAP facilitates communication with national authorities, provides assessment results, inventories and environmental management planning outputs developed under the MedProgramme, and supports the follow-up of critical approvals such as HSSE plans and Basel Notifications. UNOPS leads on technical validation, development of specifications for waste collection and disposal, procurement of contractors, and operational coordination on the ground. During the implementation phase, UNEP/MAP supports monitoring through a national expert in Montenegro, ensuring close coordination with government authorities and timely resolution of any challenges that may affect project delivery.

Together, these two activities strengthen Montenegro’s capacity to assess, manage and remediate chemical pollution hotspots, contribute to the environmentally sound management of PCBs, and support the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals related to chemicals and waste management, human health, water quality and marine protection.

projects.name: Circular Transition and Responsible Business Conduct in Montenegro (UNDP part)
projects.description:
The overarching goal of the project is to enhance Montenegro’s circular economy by fostering the application of responsible business conduct at the enterprise level, encouraging industrial symbiosis, a collaborative approach where businesses utilize waste and by-products from their processes. This approach seeks to address critical challenges of decent work at the enterprise level, including inefficient resource use, high waste generation, and limited awareness of circular economy principles among stakeholders. By promoting resource-sharing, reducing environmental impacts, and improving economic efficiency, the project directly aligns with Montenegro’s national development priorities, EU accession goals (particularly Chapter 27 on environmental protection), and global commitments under the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Paris Agreement.  
The envisaged Outcome is an increased adoption of industrial symbiosis practices and RBC/HRDD frameworks across selected clusters and MSMEs in Montenegro, ensuring gender-responsive benefits
This project will drive industrial symbiosis and circular supply chain integration by equipping MSMEs with digital tools, capacity-building programs, and policy support to enhance better working conditions for workers, resource efficiency, and MSME productivity.  
The outcome is envisaged to be achieved through three complementary project outputs that will be implemented in close collaboration between UNDP and ILO.

projects.name: Public and Private Finance for Development (PPFD) program - ReWaste – Reducing Waste and Rethinking Waste Management in Montenegro
projects.description:
In 2025, UNDP Montenegro launched the ReWaste Project under the regional Public and Private Finance for Development (PPFD) initiative, focusing on sustainable waste management. Waste management remains a critical issue for Montenegro, particularly under Chapter 27 of its EU accession process, which mandates improved waste separation, recycling, and infrastructure modernization. Despite progress, the country faces challenges, including low recycling rates, financial constraints, and inefficient landfill dependency. The ReWaste Project directly addresses these issues by modernizing waste infrastructure, enhancing institutional capacity, and fostering private and public investments to accelerate Montenegro’s transition towards a circular economy.
OBJECTIVES
The ReWaste Project seeks to transform Podgorica’s waste management system into a sustainable, modern, and EU-compliant model. The project focuses on three key areas:
•	Optimizing Waste Management Operations: Enhancing institutional efficiency, financial sustainability, and knowledge exchange with Slovak experts.
•	Attracting Investments for Infrastructure: Developing feasibility studies and investment plans to modernize waste processing facilities.
•	Promoting Public Awareness & Participation: Engaging citizens and businesses in waste separation and recycling through digital incentives and behavioural change campaigns.

projects.name: Technical and expert support to the Ministry of Justice to secure access to state funded free legal aid scheme for vulnerable persons and group of persons
projects.description: As per the 2011 Law on Free Legal Aid, state funded free legal aid covers a number of court procedures for socially vulnerable persons, but it does not cover judicial procedure for determination of date and place of birth of persons born at home, as well as all administrative procedures, including refugee status determination procedure and statelessness determination procedure. Refugees and persons missing birth registration are among the most vulnerable groups of persons in Montenegro, who often does not speak Montenegrin language and live on margins of society. Due to that reason, the Law on Free Legal Aid needs to be amended to introduce above mentioned specific procedures in the state funded free legal aid scheme. In addition, a tailor made information material needs to be produced to introduce these categories of persons with the benefits and possibilities of the state funded free legal aid scheme in procedures that they need to initiate. On that way Montenegro will implement recommendations of the UN Committee against torture, issued in the 2022 report on Montenegro. In 2025, the UN Human Rights Committee recommended to Montenegro to amend the Law on Free Legal Aid to introduce birth registration, statelessness determination and refugee status determination procedures in the state funded free legal aid system. Also, the Law should be amended to enable state funding to NGOs registered for provision of free legal aid.

projects.name: Support to creating preconditions for implementation of the LEADER approach
projects.description:
The National Program for the Development of Agriculture and Rural Areas in Montenegro under IPARD III, along with the expected adaptation in 2024 of the amendment of the Law on Agriculture and Rural Development, lays the path for the full introduction of the EU LEADER approach and should prepare the grounds for future registration of LAGs in Montenegro. However, as the country is taking the first steps towards the implementation of LEADER in accordance with the EU policy and legislation, there is a lack of technical and administrative capacity to implement it. Thus, it is necessary to strengthen capacity and knowledge on national and local levels in order to make Montenegro ready for the implementation of the EU LEADER approach. 

FAO Action aims to strengthen capacities and enabling environment at national and local levels to implement the LEADER approach and establish Local Action Groups for the benefit of increased competitiveness and economic development in rural areas of Montenegro. The project is designed to prepare the Montenegrin rural actors for implementation of LEADER approach both at the national and local levels, specifically through capacity building for LAGs creation and functioning.

projects.name: Support with the integration of an ecosystem approach to fisheries management in Skadar Lake
projects.description:
As EU candidate countries, both Albania and Montenegro are required to align with the EU Water Framework Directive, which mandates maintaining or restoring good ecological status in the lake. 
Efforts to implement modern and sustainable management of fisheries resources are hindered by administrative, technical, and financial constraints. These challenges are further complicated by the lake's cross-border status, as effective management requires cooperation between Montenegrin and Albanian authorities to align environmental standards and regulatory measures.
The requested assistance would address these gaps by strengthening transboundary cooperation and supporting the development of a simplified framework for a fishery monitoring system. This initiative aligns with national objectives facilitating Montenegro's and Albanian’s commitment to environmental sustainability and rural economic development which will in turn support the countries in their accession to EU by aligning with EU standards and practices. The project would integrate gender-sensitive practices by involving local communities, including women, in decision-making processes. The Blue Transformation roadmap recognizes the importance of aquatic food systems as drivers of employment, economic growth, social development and environmental recovery, which all underpin the SDGs.
Overall, the FAO's support in strengthening bilateral institutional collaboration under the Cooperation agreement in the fields of maintenance and joint management of fisheries in Lake Skadar and the river Bojana, and establishment of simplified monitoring system would provide the necessary technical support for the sustainable management of Skadar Lake’s fisheries, directly contributing to the long-term socio-economic resilience of local communities and environmental preservation in the region. The project thus serves the objectives of FAO Blue Transformation efforts aiming at promoting sustainable and resilient aquatic food systems.

projects.name: Support Ministry of the Interior to amend the Law on Foreigners, and harmonize other legislation accordingly
projects.description: In 2022 Montenegro started to amend its Law on Foreigners to strengthen the statelessness determination procedure, as well as other issues relevant for persons of concern to UNHCR, such as: issuing of visas for a person in family reunification procedure; access to labor market for persons granted international protection; etc. In addition, number of laws needs to be harmonized with the Law on Foreigners, to recognize stateless persons as beneficiaries of that law, thus creating condition for effective access to rights for persons granted stateless status. The draft amendments to the law has been prepared by the MoI, through cooperation with UNHCR. The draft Law is expected to be adopted in early 2026.

projects.name: Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration (AVRR)
projects.description: Within the Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration (AVRR) programme, IOM works with national and international partners in both, the host country and the country of origin, to ensure that beneficiaries willing to return to their countries of origin are able to travel in a safe and dignified manner - from host country to their final destination in country of origin.  Beneficiaries will be supported to return to their country of origin by organizing all travel arrangements including flight bookings, facilitating the issuance of travel documents when required in cooperation with the authorities of origin and/or host countries, carrying out airport clearance and other procedures as necessary, making transit and reception arrangements, facilitating pre-migration health checks, informing migrants of their travel schedules and entitlements (return allowances, luggage allowances). Additionally, upon their return to the country of origin, based on criteria associated with reintegration needs and vulnerability, beneficiaries are provided with tailored reintegration assistance in an individualized, timely and effective manner. Those not provided with reintegration assistance will continue to receive counselling and onward referral where feasible.

2) standardization of human-centered e-services and further development of digital skills of the citizens and businesses, reflected in the Output 2 - Increased digital efficiency of public administration serving citizens and businesses.

Technical and expert support to the Administrative Court of Montenegro, Bar Association and Ombudsperson to work with asylum seekers, refugees and stateless persons/persons at risk of statelessness
projects.description: The Administrative Court of Montenegro is the 2nd instance institution in the asylum procedures and the 3rd instance institution in the statelessness determination procedure. Work with asylum seekers, refugees and stateless persons/persons at risk of statelessness pose different challenges to the court: from interpretation services, to more specific knowledge on different topics (country of origin information, unaccompanied and separated children, family reunification cases, credibility assessment, etc.). During 2023-2025, UNHCR organized several workshops for judges of the Administrative Court and the Bar Association, to facilitate discussion on several asylum related topics. The Ombudsperson is the main national human rights institution whose role in access to territory and detention facilities is of utmost importance for asylum seekers, refugees and stateless persons/persons at risk of statelessness. In 2024, UNHCR and the Ombudsperson renewed Memorandum of Understanding to define cooperation in the area of joint interest, such as border monitoring.

projects.name: Support line institutions to improve the standards in access to territory and asylum procedure in line with the UNHCR's and Montenegrin Ombudsman's findings from the 2022/23 partnership projects
projects.description: While Montenegro is a positive example in the region in relation to access to territory, the Ombudsman/UNHCR projects implemented in 2022 and 2023 provided clear indicators on where the focus should be put in the following period. As the outcome, the Border Police of Montenegro and UNHCR posted a 6-languages poster (Montenegrin, English, Arabic, Farsi, Russian and Spanish) in all sea/land/air border crossings, with information to interested persons on possibility to apply for asylum in Montenegro. The poster contains QR code that leads to UNHCR hotline and HELP page, containing additional information on asylum system of Montenegro and assistance that a person can get if s/he decides to apply for asylum. In addition, the Border Police opened possibility for registration of asylum intention in all police stations in Montenegro, in line with the 2018 asylum law. Other Ombudsman's recommendations, related to capacity building of Border Police, will be included in UNHCR's training and advocacy activities.

projects.name: Facilitate the certificate recognition for refugees to ensure that their prior learning was recognized and valorized in education and employment
projects.description:
Following UNHCR's advocacy efforts, the Ministry of Education, Science, and Innovation prepared amendments to the Law on Recognition of Foreign Diplomas and Qualifications, adopted by the Parliament in 2025. These amendments are opening possibility for adoption of by-law to the amended Law, to secure that refugees cannot always obtain all the documents necessary for the recognition of foreign diplomas as required by regular procedures. During 2026, UNHCR expects to work with the education ministry on the above mentioned by-law.
Consequently, the Ministry of Education has started collaborating with the Council of Europe to determine the manner of establishing qualifications and skills for refugees who do not possess the respective educational certificates (prior test). UNHCR will continue to make significant effort to contribute to the adoption of this procedure.

projects.name: Ending the Denial of Legal Capacity of Persons with Disabilities in Montenegro
projects.description: The programme seeks to facilitate system-level change in Montenegro by proposing amendments to a legal framework that violates rights and by establishing a system that supports persons with disabilities to exercise their rights. It seeks to address harmful practices and significantly reduce cases of legal capacity denial for persons with disabilities. Thereby, it will end the discrimination persons with disabilities face and empower them to exercise their human rights. A new service for supported decision-making will be designed and piloted to drive system-level change. The project will establish a scalable model to enable persons with disabilities, particularly those with intellectual and psychosocial disabilities, to access structured, sustainable support mechanisms that enable them to make decisions on an equal basis with others.

projects.name: Enhancing citizens’ trust in institutions and building resilient communities (Joint PBF project)
projects.description:
The UNDP component of the Joint UN Programme aims to foster trust in institutions and build resilient communities by enhancing social cohesion and promoting gender equality. It emphasizes the empowerment of both women and men, particularly younger generations, to engage in meaningful civic activities that protect human rights and advance social cohesion. Key activities include organizing local dialogues in five communities to address trust issues, divisive narratives, and social cohesion, and designing actionable recommendations.

A Social Cohesion Innovation Lab will pilot solutions developed during these dialogues, working with civil society and local governments. Institutional capacities at local and national levels will be strengthened to develop, adopt, and implement pledges for social cohesion, informed by local dialogue outcomes. The initiative also supports parliaments at both the national and local levels to enhance oversight and promote dialogue on social cohesion.

The program aims to monitor hate speech, violence, and divisive narratives, building capacity for evidence-based policymaking using behavioral insights and public perception surveys. It includes advocacy to counter hate speech and foster trust and collaboration. Additionally, the program empowers women politicians and decision-makers with skills and knowledge to advance gender equality and address gender-based challenges effectively.
